idiom_name: one function per rule over a discriminated token union with exhaustive narrowing
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds compile-time structure to the JavaScript parser without changing its runtime shape: tokens are a discriminated union ({ kind: 'plus' } | { kind: 'name'; text: string } | ...), and switch/narrowing on the kind gives exhaustive dispatch checked by the compiler, while rules stay ordinary functions over a token array. What replaces the classic structure is the type system - the token union is the grammar's alphabet written down once and the never-check keeps dispatch total - and the compiler API (ts.createSourceFile, ts.SyntaxKind, forEachChild) exposes the TypeScript compiler's own trees, which is what you want when the input is TypeScript or JavaScript rather than your own grammar. Keep this form for grammars you own; reach for the compiler API for TS/JS analysis.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: a switch with an else branch or a cast defeats the exhaustiveness guarantee, so keep the token union closed and let never-checks fail the build.
Deep recursion still overflows the JavaScript engine stack - TypeScript cannot protect the runtime - so untrusted input needs an explicit depth guard.
ts.createSourceFile parses TypeScript/JavaScript only and cannot be pointed at your own grammar; its SyntaxKind enum is a compiler detail, not a general parser toolkit.

variants.name: Chevrotain LL(k) grammar (TypeScript API)
variants.idiom_name: chevrotain typed token vocabulary + rule methods with computed lookahead
variants.implementation_notes: Chevrotain is written in TypeScript and its API is typed end to end: the token vocabulary is declared with createToken, rules are methods that consume tokens and call sub-rules, and performSelfAnalysis computes lookahead functions, validates the grammar and produces a positioned CST with recovery - no code generation, grammars are ordinary TS sources. Choose it when a larger grammar needs mechanical lookahead management, grammar validation and recovery, and when the typed rule API is worth a dependency; the hand-written variant remains the baseline for small grammars and dependency-free tools.
pitfalls: performSelfAnalysis is per parser class, not per parse, and must run after every RULE property is assigned; calling it twice throws and calling it early yields misleading lookahead errors.
The grammar is validated against the token vocabulary at analysis time, so an ambiguous or left-recursive rule fails there - the grammar must be LL(k) or refactored with explicit lookahead.
